title: Learned activity models improve viral diagnostic assay designs
summary: Learned diagnostic-activity scores guided assay design across viral variation. Experiments on selected synthetic targets supported improved detection compared with the studied conservation-based designs. The larger cross-species design catalog is computational; it is not thousands of validated diagnostics. Patient-specimen sensitivity, clinical specificity and field performance were not established.
ai_technology: ADAPT learned sequence-activity classifier and regressor
organization: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; Massachusetts Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: Selected assay designs were tested on synthetic viral targets.
evidence.unknown: Clinical and environmental sample performance require further validation.
evidence.ai_role: ADAPT learned sequence-activity classifier and regressor supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.
